assumptions: The lender is an Italian bank or an Article 106 financial intermediary.
The borrower is a natural person and the product is consumer or mortgage credit.
The lender uses credit-information systems and AI or automated processing in credit assessment.
exclusions: Entity-specific supervisory decisions and licence conditions.
Tax, employment, accounting, company-law, and product rules unrelated to credit assessment.
Business lending, servicing of non-performing loans, securitisation, insurance distribution, and payment services unless separately scoped.

entries.title: Mortgage creditworthiness assessment
entries.applicability: Consumer credit relating to residential immovable property.
entries.obligation: Carry out a thorough creditworthiness assessment using necessary, sufficient, proportionate, and appropriately verified economic and financial information before concluding the credit agreement.
open_credit_evidence: Trace each material summary fact to verified source information.
Flag missing or contradictory income, expense, debt, and repayment-capacity facts.

entries.title: Thorough consumer creditworthiness assessment
entries.applicability: Consumer credit within TUB Title VI, Chapter II, subject to statutory exclusions and transition rules.
entries.obligation: Assess the consumer's creditworthiness thoroughly before concluding the credit agreement, including in the consumer's interest to avoid irresponsible lending and over-indebtedness.
open_credit_evidence: Verify that the internal summary contains all defined decision-critical facts.
Record omissions before the lending decision proceeds.
entries.notes: General adaptation deadline: 20 November 2026 or, if later, 90 days after the relevant Bank of Italy implementing provisions enter into force.

entries.title: Necessary and proportionate creditworthiness information
entries.applicability: Consumer creditworthiness assessments under Article 124-bis.
entries.obligation: Use necessary and proportionate economic and financial information, appropriately verify it, exclude GDPR special-category data, and do not treat social networks as external sources.
open_credit_evidence: Record the source document for each critical fact.
Restrict materiality rules to decision-relevant economic and financial information.
Flag prohibited source or data categories before processing.

entries.title: Documented and updated assessment procedures
entries.applicability: Lenders carrying out consumer creditworthiness assessments.
entries.obligation: Develop, document, and keep creditworthiness-assessment procedures and the information used by those procedures up to date.
open_credit_evidence: Version materiality rules and checker logic.
Record the rule and checker version on each evidence report.
Maintain a change history and periodic review record.

entries.title: Explanation of automated creditworthiness assessment
entries.applicability: A creditworthiness assessment based even partly on automated processing of the consumer's personal data.
entries.obligation: On request, provide a clear and understandable explanation of the creditworthiness assessment, including the logic and risks of the automated processing and its significance and effects on the decision.
open_credit_evidence: Preserve the observed facts used in the internal summary.
Separate observed facts from inferences.
Provide traceable supporting evidence for a lender-created explanation.
entries.notes: OpenCredit's internal completeness report is supporting evidence, not the legally required consumer-facing explanation.

entries.title: Consumer opportunity to express a view
entries.applicability: A creditworthiness assessment based even partly on automated processing of the consumer's personal data.
entries.obligation: Allow the consumer to express their view to the lender.
open_credit_evidence: Link consumer-provided corrections or context to the case evidence.
Re-run materiality checks when relevant source information changes.

entries.title: Human reconsideration of assessment and decision
entries.applicability: A creditworthiness assessment based even partly on automated processing of the consumer's personal data.
entries.obligation: Provide a route for reconsideration by the lender of both the creditworthiness assessment and the credit-granting decision.
open_credit_evidence: Show the reviewer the checked summary, omissions, and source evidence.
Record the human outcome, override, reason, and timestamp.

entries.title: Third-party explanation information
entries.applicability: The lender uses a third party to perform automated processing involved in the creditworthiness assessment.
entries.obligation: Obtain from the third party the information needed to provide the consumer with the required explanation.
open_credit_evidence: Expose versioned model, prompt, checker, and source-use information to the lender.
Link OpenCredit and model-provider evidence to the same lender process instance.

entries.title: Advance notice of automated processing rights
entries.applicability: The lender will use automated processing of personal data in the creditworthiness assessment.
entries.obligation: Inform the consumer of the human-intervention, explanation, view, and reconsideration rights before automated processing begins, including relevant third-party involvement.
open_credit_evidence: Expose accurate system and third-party identification for the lender's notice.
Record the notice version and acknowledgement in the host workflow.

entries.title: Information following credit rejection
entries.applicability: A consumer credit application is rejected.
entries.obligation: Inform the consumer promptly of the rejection and, where relevant, that automated processing was used, the applicable intervention rights, and the reconsideration procedure.
open_credit_evidence: Provide verified decision inputs for an accurate rejection communication.
Do not transform the internal summary into an applicant explanation without lender review.

entries.title: Prohibited data for creditworthiness assessment
entries.applicability: Lenders and credit intermediaries assessing consumer creditworthiness.
entries.obligation: Do not process GDPR special-category data or personal data obtained from social networks for creditworthiness assessment.
open_credit_evidence: Reject prohibited source categories before summary generation.
Record allowed source types without reproducing unnecessary personal data.

entries.title: Accuracy and correction of credit-database information
entries.applicability: A lender communicates consumer information to covered credit databases.
entries.obligation: Ensure information communicated to credit databases is accurate and current and promptly correct errors.
open_credit_evidence: Detect contradictions between source documents and case metadata.
Version corrected source material and invalidate superseded summaries.

entries.title: Automated creditworthiness rights for financing contracts
entries.applicability: Covered financing contracts where the customer's creditworthiness assessment relies even partly on automated processing of personal data.
entries.obligation: Apply the Article 124-bis automated-assessment intervention, explanation, view, reconsideration, notice, and rejection protections to the covered assessment.
open_credit_evidence: Use the applicable Article 124-bis obligation IDs for the evidence report.
Preserve the connection between technical evidence and the lender's human-review process.

entries.title: Private credit-information systems Code of Conduct
entries.citation: Garante Privacy decision no. 163 of 12 September 2019 and attached Code of Conduct
entries.applicability: Participation in or use of private credit-information systems concerning consumer credit, reliability, and payment punctuality.
entries.obligation: Apply sector rules covering lawful purposes, data categories, notices, accuracy, negative-data warnings, retention periods, access, correction, and monitoring.
open_credit_evidence: Identify the credit-information source and observation date.
Keep source facts distinct from inference.
Support correction and regeneration when source data changes.

entries.title: Central Credit Register reporting instructions
entries.citation: Bank of Italy Circular no. 139 of 11 February 1991, as amended
entries.applicability: Intermediaries participating in or using the Bank of Italy Central Credit Register.
entries.obligation: Use Central Credit Register data only for permitted credit-risk purposes, apply the reporting and correction rules, and account for the limitations of the returned data.
open_credit_evidence: Label Central Credit Register facts as non-certificative source data.
Record reporting period and provenance.
Avoid unsupported conclusions from incomplete system coverage.

entries.title: Transparency and fairness in banking and financial services
entries.citation: Bank of Italy provisions of 29 July 2009, as amended
entries.applicability: Banks and financial intermediaries offering banking and financial products and services in Italy.
entries.obligation: Provide clear, accurate, comprehensible, and consistent information and maintain fair customer relations, complaints handling, and required product and contract disclosures.
open_credit_evidence: Use precise, source-grounded language in internal summaries.
Prevent internal evidence artifacts from being presented as consumer disclosures without review.

entries.title: Italian artificial intelligence law
entries.applicability: Research, development, adoption, and use of AI systems and models in Italy, interpreted consistently with the EU AI Act.
entries.obligation: Apply the national principles of human-centric, transparent, responsible, secure, accurate, non-discriminatory, and privacy-protective AI and the Italian governance framework.
open_credit_evidence: Document human oversight, traceability, data protection, accuracy, and non-discrimination evidence.
Do not present the law as creating a separate OpenCredit certification.
entries.notes: Article 3(5) states that the law does not create new obligations for AI systems or general-purpose AI models beyond the EU AI Act.

entries.title: Italian Personal Data Protection Code
entries.applicability: Processing of personal data in Italy alongside the GDPR.
entries.obligation: Apply Italian data-protection provisions, safeguards, remedies, and enforcement rules in addition to directly applicable GDPR duties.
open_credit_evidence: Minimise personal data in evidence reports.
Apply retention, access, security, correction, and rights-handling controls defined by the lender.

entries.title: Italian Banking Act regulatory perimeter
entries.applicability: Banks, Article 106 financial intermediaries, credit intermediaries, and covered banking and credit activities according to their specific TUB status.
entries.obligation: Meet the applicable authorisation, governance, prudential, transparency, customer-protection, reporting, and supervisory requirements.
open_credit_evidence: Record the regulated entity type and product before selecting obligation IDs.

entries.title: Bank of Italy supervisory provisions for banks
entries.citation: Bank of Italy Circular no. 285 of 17 December 2013, as amended
entries.applicability: Banks within the scope of the Bank of Italy supervisory provisions.
entries.obligation: Apply the relevant governance, internal-control, risk-management, outsourcing, information-system, and prudential requirements.
open_credit_evidence: Integrate OpenCredit governance with the lender's model, ICT, outsourcing, and internal-control framework.

entries.title: Bank of Italy supervisory provisions for financial intermediaries
entries.citation: Bank of Italy Circular no. 288 of 3 April 2015, as amended
entries.applicability: Financial intermediaries entered in the register under TUB Article 106.
entries.obligation: Apply the relevant authorisation, governance, internal-control, risk-management, organisational, and prudential requirements.
open_credit_evidence: Integrate OpenCredit governance with the intermediary's internal-control and risk-management framework.

entries.title: Anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing
entries.applicability: Obliged lenders and financial intermediaries under Italian AML law.
entries.obligation: Apply customer due diligence, beneficial-owner identification, risk assessment, recordkeeping, suspicious-transaction reporting, internal controls, and applicable restrictions.
open_credit_evidence: Keep AML determinations outside the materiality checker unless expressly included in the lender's authorised use case.
Avoid exposing AML-sensitive information in summary evidence.

entries.title: Anti-usury limits
entries.citation: Law no. 108 of 7 March 1996 and quarterly threshold decrees
entries.applicability: Financing transactions subject to Italian anti-usury rules.
entries.obligation: Ensure the effective rate and relevant charges do not exceed the applicable category- and amount-specific quarterly threshold.
open_credit_evidence: Do not describe pricing as lawful without a separate time-specific threshold calculation.

entries.title: Italian Consumer Code
entries.applicability: Consumer-facing lending conduct, marketing, contracting, digital interfaces, and commercial practices where the Consumer Code applies.
entries.obligation: Avoid unfair or misleading commercial practices and apply applicable consumer information, contracting, and remedy requirements.
open_credit_evidence: Do not reuse an internal credit summary as consumer marketing or disclosure copy without separate legal and factual review.

entries.title: Banking and Financial Ombudsman redress framework
entries.citation: Bank of Italy provisions on out-of-court resolution of banking and financial disputes, as amended
entries.applicability: Banks and other covered financial intermediaries in disputes concerning banking and financial operations and services.
entries.obligation: Maintain complaint handling and participate in the applicable Banking and Financial Ombudsman framework, including disputes about loans and credit-register reporting.
open_credit_evidence: Preserve the evidence report and human-review history needed to investigate a complaint.
Support correction and re-evaluation without treating the report as a final legal determination.
